answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before influencing shared reputation. The system counts trust only when actions are confirmed over time by independently staked counterparts, so new identities cannot gain standing by echo alone. To sway outcomes, an attacker must fund every identity and keep its stake exposed through the observation period. Coordinating a vine of accounts multiplies that capital requirement, while detected collusion can slash the stakes, making recovery from the resulting dune expensive.
